Owner decisions on the M11 security review (2026-11-25, "all as recommended"): RDP now requires NLA (CredSSP) and refuses a TLS-only or standard-security server with `nla_required`, so an old host without NLA no longer connects until the backlog item "RDP: allow servers without NLA per connection" is built; the release workflow attests build provenance of the installers (first exercised on the v0.3.0 release run); the remaining risks of findings rows 22, 35, 36, 37, 38, 40, 41, 42, 45, 51, 55, 56, 57, 62, 68 and 75 are accepted (recorded in `Docs/DECISIONS.md` "M11: owner decisions on the security review (2026-11-25)"); four behaviour changes are acknowledged (a rotated host key raises the changed-key prompt on the other devices, symlinked data files are refused, release builds refuse a plain `http://` hub, a repeated JSON key makes a file unreadable); the repo settings (required reviews on `dev`, SHA pinning and CodeQL for `actions`, a `v*` tag ruleset, immutable releases) stay the owner's and are named in the readiness section of `Docs/release-checklist.md`. scopeChanges.context: Roadmap extended (M13 to M21, v0.4.0 to v0.6.0)
scopeChanges.text: Owner request: automatic updates, and a security check plus release-readiness milestone before every release. The roadmap gains three releases and nine milestones. Every release is preceded by its own gate milestone (M14, M17, M21) that updates the threat model, reviews each changed area independently, runs `/security-review` and the dependency checks, triages findings in `Docs/release-checklist.md`, lists the open owner checks and ends with a go or no-go verdict; the gate prepares the release and does not perform it. Not every milestone is a release: v0.4.0 covers M13 and M14, v0.5.0 covers M15 to M17, v0.6.0 covers M18 to M21. M13 (automatic updates) takes "Narrow the webview capability" from the backlog because the update commands touch the same capability file. Code signing and notarisation is not scheduled: the owner finds it too expensive, so the backlog item stays (reworded: the Windows part has a free route for open-source projects, the macOS part needs the paid Apple Developer Program) and the installers stay unsigned; the update signature of M13 is separate and free. M15 and M16 take "Export to mRemoteNG format" and "SFTP file browser", M18 and M19 take "Split panes and detached tabs" (detached windows only if the spec finds a safe way), "Broadcast input" and "Local shell tabs", and M20 takes the hardening items of the M11 review that were accepted for later ("Forget a host key", "Detect a frozen SSH tab", "Native confirmation for sync setup and join", "Sync key rotation", "RDP: allow servers without NLA per connection", "Note when auto-lock is off because settings.json is unusable"). The owner swapped jump hosts and port forwarding out of M15 for the mRemoteNG export, so "Port forwarding and jump hosts" stays in the backlog. The order of M15 to M19 follows the owner’s expected daily use and can be changed before a milestone is planned. A version that contains the updater cannot update older installs, so v0.4.0 is installed by hand once and the first real update is v0.4.0 to v0.5.0 (an owner check in M17).

Decisions while planning M13 (design `superpowers/specs/2026-11-26-m13-auto-update-design.md`, plan `superpowers/plans/2026-11-26-milestone-13-auto-update.md`): the update files are signed in a separate `sign` job that is the only holder of the signing key (an extra `verify-signatures` job without secrets checks every signature against the pinned public key before `publish`), not in a step of the build job; `bundle.createUpdaterArtifacts` stays off because it makes `tauri build` demand the key, so the macOS tarball is packed by a script; there are six commands, not three (`update_status`, `update_check`, `update_install`, `update_skip`, `set_check_for_updates`, `update_open_release_page`); the download is confirmed after it finished (the app stays usable while it runs) and capped at 256 MiB; the "exactly one GET" check counts the redirect hops of that one request, because GitHub answers release downloads with a redirect to its asset host; `latest.json` is written by `tools/write-latest-json.mjs` (Node, JSON); the first real update from a released version waits for the M17 gate, because v0.4.0 is the first build with an updater, so M13 proves the path against a test feed.

Changes against the planning text found while building M13 (details in `Docs/DECISIONS.md` "M13: update feed, signing job, key lifecycle and scope changes"): `update_open_release_page` takes no argument and falls back to the generic releases page (`https://github.com/benjo-code/fernjo/releases/latest`, built in Rust) when no version is on offer, so every failed state can offer "Open release page"; the owner delivered the real public key, so there is no placeholder key and no release guard for one; `plugins.updater` sets `requireSignedVersion: true` and the sign job passes `--app-version`, so a signature is bound to its version; the `update-test-hooks` feature is switched on for the package's own tests through a self dev-dependency, so `cargo test --workspace` runs the fake-feed tests; `ci.yml` also runs `cargo clippy -p fernjo-app --lib --bins -- -D warnings` (the shipped feature-off configuration); the real-build capability check could not run on the development machine and stays an owner check with a static proof recorded; the task about the signing key stays open until the owner has put the key and password into the Environment `release-signing`, which must exist with its protection before the first tag.

The final review of the M13 branch added to the milestone: the test-feed configuration for the owner checks that the design (section 8) asks for is now part of M13 (`tools/update-test.conf.json`, the steps in `Docs/release-checklist.md` "Update check against a local test feed", guard tests that keep it out of a release; `tools/write-latest-json.mjs` got no URL override). Also fixed: a skipped version hides its notice, the dialog says "Hide" while downloading, a check from "ready" keeps the held download installable, the window cannot be closed while installing, and a panic in an update step no longer leaves the run slot taken. Details in `Docs/DECISIONS.md` "M13: final review fixes". The owner checks stay open.

scopeChanges.context: M13 owner decisions after the merge
scopeChanges.text: Owner decision: the updater is not checked by hand against a local test feed but with the real feed, when the release after the first one with the updater (v0.4.0) comes out. The two manual criteria of M13 (update on Windows, macOS and a Linux AppImage; release page offer for a `.deb` and a read-only AppImage) and the "update window opens" part of the capability criterion move to the acceptance of v0.5.0, or of an earlier follow-up release. Accepted cost: if the updater of v0.4.0 does not work somewhere, that install needs one manual reinstall to get the fix. `tools/update-test.conf.json` and its steps in `Docs/release-checklist.md` stay, as an optional check. The signing key task now says what is true: the owner keeps a copy of the private key outside GitHub (the M13 design wants it off any developer machine's disk after set-up; where the copy lives is not recorded). Follow-up fixes after the merge: the tests of `verify_update_signature` run with `cargo test --workspace`, and "Restart now" or a late close confirmation is dropped while an update installs.

The capability criterion was reworded when it was checked: "Check now" cannot show that `update-status` arrives, because the screen also follows the command's reply, so the event proof is the `vault-status` event after the idle auto-lock (same permission). The check was run by hand with the installer of a release dry run instead of the DevTools-port recipe on a `--no-bundle` binary.

Decisions while planning M14 (design `superpowers/specs/2026-11-27-m14-security-gate-v0.4.0-design.md`, plan `superpowers/plans/2026-11-27-milestone-14-security-gate.md`): added are a Windows test job in CI (no test of the M13 updater had run on Windows), the owner's key copy check and a local rehearsal of the signing and publishing commands with the test key (signing, signature verification and `latest.json` have never run on GitHub; a rehearsal on GitHub was rejected because it needs the tag-only rule of the `release-signing` environment loosened). The release gate takes its dry run on the milestone's final head, and the version bump and version check stay with the release branch. Known mismatch left for the planning of M17: its task and criterion say an installed v0.4.0 updates to a v0.5.0 candidate through a test feed, but a released v0.4.0 only reads the real GitHub feed (no runtime override), so that run needs the published release, as the v0.5.0 release criterion already says.

blocks.title: Source: Confirm quit with live sessions
blocks.text: Closing the window while sessions are connected ends them without asking. Ask for confirmation when at least one session is connected (M4 only confirms when a single connected tab is closed).

blocks.title: Source: Settings dialog: wrong "not saved" note when settings.json is unusable
blocks.text: The note "not saved while FERNJO_DATA_DIR is set" also appears when `settings.json` is unreadable or from a newer version, where it is wrong: nothing is saved there either, but the reason is the unusable file, not the environment variable (pre-existing from M4; the theme section copies it). Fix: tell the two states apart (the `persistent` flag plus the unusable-settings state, `AppState.settings_unusable`, which the UI may need to be told about) and show a message that names the real cause.

blocks.title: Source: Separate timeout for agents that need a confirmation
blocks.text: The agent sign step shares the connect timeout (15 s), so an agent that asks for a touch or a confirmation per signature (hardware key, `ssh-add -c`) can time out while the user is still deciding. Give the sign step its own, longer limit, or pause the clock like the prompts do.

blocks.title: Source: connections.json lost update when a sync tool delivers a newer file
blocks.text: The app keeps the tree in memory and rewrites `connections.json` on every change, so a file that Syncthing, Nextcloud or Dropbox delivers while the app runs is overwritten and the other device's edits are lost. The vault already guards against this (M3: `Vault::save` re-reads the file and refuses with `changed_on_disk` unless it still starts with the header the handle last read or wrote). Apply the same check-then-write idea to the tree: remember a fingerprint (for example a hash or the length and modification time) of the last bytes read or written, compare it before saving, and refuse or offer to reload when the file changed. It stays a check, not a lock, so a sync tool can still win the race between check and rename.

blocks.title: Source: What is the WebView2 background connection?
blocks.text: From M6 security review finding 5. About 60 s after start the Windows WebView2 runtime (not fernjo.exe) opens one HTTPS connection to an address registered to Microsoft; its purpose is not verified and `--disable-background-networking` did not stop it. Find out what it is and whether a WebView2 setting turns it off; check macOS and Linux too. The README privacy statement says what is known today.

blocks.title: Source: Remove build paths from release binaries
blocks.text: From M6 security review finding 6. CI-built binaries embed the runner's cargo registry paths in panic locations (`C:\Users\runneradmin\.cargo\registry\...`, `/home/runner/.cargo/...`, `/Users/runner/.cargo/...`); no personal name occurs in any installer. Set `RUSTFLAGS=--remap-path-prefix` in `release.yml` if the paths should disappear.

blocks.title: Source: Vault Low findings
blocks.text: From the M6 independent vault review (`Docs/release-checklist.md`, finding 17). Attacker-chosen KDF cost accepted at load (1 GiB, 20 passes, 16 lanes: about 15 s per unlock attempt; backups the same, 16.7 s); the temp file name is fixed, followed through symlinks, no `create_new`, no directory fsync; the Windows keychain item uses "Enterprise" persistence by default (credential roaming); secret residue in freed buffers (`normalise`, `save`, plain `[u8; 32]` copies, the argon2 matrix); `change_password` never upgrades the KDF cost; the header is re-encoded from parsed fields (a trap when `CURRENT_VERSION` becomes 2); the public `Secret` derives `Serialize`. Related: `connections.json` and `settings.json` are read without a size cap.

blocks.title: Source: SSH Low findings
blocks.text: From the M6 independent SSH review (`Docs/release-checklist.md`, finding 18). `known_hosts` `replace` removes only the first matching entry of a line, so a hand-edited `h,H` line leaves the old key trusted; a key of another algorithm for a stored host reads as a new host (a legitimate key-type rotation fails with a generic protocol error); `@revoked` lines are ignored (documented); `known_hosts` writes use a fixed temp name, no `create_new` and no cross-session lock; server keyboard-interactive text and prompt count are unbounded in the UI; secrets are copied into plain `String`s for the wire; no host key re-check on re-key (russh); Windows agent pipe squatting (same as OpenSSH for Windows).

blocks.title: Source: Import and backup Low findings
blocks.text: From the M6 independent import review (`Docs/release-checklist.md`, finding 19). Unbounded attacker strings reach the webview in error messages and in backup `createdAt` and `app`; the export-target guard covers only the data folder (not the config folder or a pending data folder); names, hosts and descriptions of the JSON and backup import paths are not validated for control characters or length (the mRemoteNG path got length caps in M6); `import_apply` holds the pending lock across the disk work while the page-load hook takes it on the UI thread (a reload during a slow save freezes the window); residual unzeroised non-secret copies. A restored backup replaces the tree and the vault entries by design, so the confirmation could name more than counts.

blocks.title: Source: M6 security fixes: deferred follow-ups
blocks.text:
From the M6 security fixes (plan `superpowers/plans/2026-11-18-milestone-06-security-fixes.md`, reviews and `Docs/release-checklist.md` findings 4, 14, 16). None blocks v0.1.0.

- Concurrent host confirmations (two sessions confirming at once) may lose an update: the confirmed-hosts file is written through a fixed `.tmp` name without a lock (fails safe: the host asks again).
- Vault rollback: two histories that reach the same generation (an equal-generation divergence) are not detected.
- A startup notice when `settings.json` holds a `dataDir` that contains the device-local folder (the folder dialog refuses it, a hand-edited `settings.json` does not).
- A host key of another type for a host the device confirmed earlier (a key-type downgrade) shows no `previous` fingerprint in the prompt.
- `Unknown` plus 'trust always' does not replace a different key of the same type in the confirmed-hosts file.

blocks.title: Source: Close the tab when the shell exits on purpose
blocks.text:
Owner request of 2026-11-18, reported while testing on macOS; for after v0.1.0 (the owner decided that this and the two items above come after the first release). It applies on all platforms. Today a session tab turns yellow ('connection lost', Reconnect) also when the user ends the shell on purpose, for example with `exit`, `logout` or Ctrl+D in a Linux terminal. Wanted: the tab closes itself after an intentional end, but stays yellow with Reconnect when the connection drops.

Design notes: the SSH server reports a deliberate shell end as a channel exit-status (or exit-signal) followed by EOF and close, whereas network loss, a keepalive timeout, a reset or a transport error carries no exit status. Rule: auto-close only for a clean exit-status; keep the tab for transport errors, timeouts and server-side disconnect messages that have an error reason. Exceptions so that nothing disappears unread: a session that ends within the first few seconds after login (for example 'Permission denied' or an error banner) stays open, and optionally a non-zero exit status stays open too. A setting 'Close the tab when the shell exits' in Settings (suggested default on, switchable off, remembered like the terminal settings in `settings.json` with the existing persistence rules). It touches the SSH session end handling in `fernjo-ssh`, the session manager (`sessions.rs`: the end-of-session event gets an `exitStatus` or 'ended cleanly' field in the wire contract described at the top of that file, rationale in `Docs/DECISIONS.md` 'M4 session IPC') and the tab logic in the UI. Tests for each ending kind; the SSH container tests (`tools/ssh-test-server.sh`) can produce `exit 0`, `exit 3` and a killed connection.

blocks.title: Source: Linux title bar icon placeholder
blocks.text:
Owner observation of 2026-11-18 on a CachyOS (Arch) laptop with the AppImage (`Docs/release-checklist.md` gap 27, Low, cosmetic): the title bar of the window shows a placeholder logo instead of the fernjo icon, while the icon in the Linux taskbar is correct. For after v0.1.0 unless the diagnostics below point to a cheap fix.

Established by the controller: `tauri-codegen` embeds as the default window icon on Linux the first `.png` of `bundle.icon` in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, which is `icons/32x32.png`, and that file is the correct fernjo icon (charcoal tile, ring, yellow dot), so the embedded window icon is right. Probable cause, not verified: the compositor looks the title bar icon up through the app id (identifier `io.github.benjo-code.fernjo`) in a `.desktop` file, which an AppImage run without desktop integration does not provide; the taskbar showing the right icon points to a different lookup.

Diagnostics for the owner: note the desktop environment and session type (Wayland or X11); run `GDK_BACKEND=x11 ./fernjo_0.0.0_amd64.AppImage` (if the title bar icon is right under X11, it is the Wayland app-id lookup); try an integrated AppImage (Gear Lever or AppImageLauncher; if it is right after integration, it is the missing desktop file of an unintegrated AppImage). Possible fixes: set the window icon explicitly in `setup` with `tauri::include_image!` and `set_icon`, or ship a `.desktop` file with the AppImage that matches the app id. If the cause is confirmed as an environment limit, add a known-limits sentence to the README.

blocks.title: Source: Discoverability and clarity of the UI (review of the whole app)
blocks.text:
Owner request of 2026-11-18, found while testing the first installed builds; for after v0.1.0. It applies on all platforms. It is related to, but separate from, the other post-v0.1.0 UI items (resizable panels, multi-select in the tree, close the tab on an intentional shell exit). The owner did not immediately find where Import/Export and Settings are, and above all did not realise that the sidebar chip showing only 'unlocked' and a padlock is the credential vault, where logins (credentials) are defined. If the owner, who knows the app, did not see it, new users will not either.

Wanted:

- Make the vault recognisable and self-explanatory: a label that says 'Vault' or what it holds, a short explanation or first-run hint for 'where do I store logins', clear locked and unlocked wording, and an obvious path from a connection's 'Credential' property to the vault manager.
- Make Import & backup, Export and Settings easier to find and name consistently (the sidebar footer today: a gear for Settings and 'Import & backup').
- A general review of the whole app for clarity: labels, empty states, first-run guidance, icons that come with text, the wording of the properties panel, discoverability of context menus, keyboard shortcuts and the session and tab actions, and confusing states (locked vault, host key prompts).

Approach: do it as a design critique with real screenshots (the `impeccable` skill; `DESIGN.md` and the tokens in `ui/src/styles/tokens.css` apply, no new visual direction), turn the findings into a short list, agree it with the owner, then implement the agreed changes with tests.

blocks.text: The "changed on disk" bar with its Reload button appears only for tree edits. blocks.title: Source: Stale vault temp files after a crash
blocks.text: `write_atomic` in the vault creates `vault.fernjo.<hex>.tmp` with a random name and removes it on failure, but a crash or kill between create and rename leaves it behind, and nothing ever sweeps these files. They hold encrypted vault bytes only and are harmless, but they accumulate in a synced folder. Remove temp files of that pattern older than a day when the vault is opened.

blocks.text: The close confirmation intercepts `CloseRequested` of the main window only. Cmd+Q on macOS leaves through `RunEvent::ExitRequested`, which is not intercepted, so connected sessions end without a question there. Intercept the event in the run callback and reuse the same dialog and `close_prompt_open` flag; see `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, "M7: close confirmation, batch move and panel layout".

blocks.text: A restored backup replaces the tree and the vault entries by design; the confirmation dialog could name more than counts (for example what is replaced and what is kept). UI wording only, no safety effect (moved back from the M7 triage of the import Low findings).

blocks.text: A keyboard-focused splitter is an opaque 6 px bar in `--color-focus`, while `DESIGN.md` defines keyboard focus as a 1 px inset outline. The vertical splitter sits at `right: -3px`, so it also covers 3 px of the tree's scrollbar edge. Draw the focus state as a 1 px line inside the 6 px hit area and move the hit area so it does not overlap the scrollbar.

blocks.title: Source: M4 review follow-ups
blocks.text:
Deferred from the whole-branch review of M4, none of them blocks the milestone:

- `SshError` carries no source (thin diagnostics); the error mapping is coarse and `io_to_lost` is misnamed.
- `known_hosts`: the BOM is lost when the first line is replaced; a duplicate host inside one entry's host list leaves a stale entry; test gaps (hashed non-22 and IPv6 hosts, tab separators, add on a CRLF file).
- `TrustAlways` and `Replace` write `known_hosts` before the key-exchange signature is verified; park the decision and write after `connect_stream` succeeds.
- A russh session task and its file descriptor leak on a pre-key-exchange timeout.
- The session input queue is unbounded; cap it (about 8 MiB).
- `tauri_plugin_opener::init()` injects an init script; use `Builder::new().open_js_links_on_click(false).build()`.
- The agent test is named "in order" but asserts only that the login works.
- Chords use `e.key` instead of `e.code`, so Ctrl+Shift chords fail on non-Latin layouts.
- Terminal: the `ResizeObserver` is not coalesced per frame, `findNext` is not incremental, the search bar hardcodes 13 px.
- Tabs: an Escape-cancelled drag still fires a click; arrow keys fire from the Close and Reconnect buttons and there is no Home, End or Delete; the tab ARIA is loose; `.reconnect` uses weight 500 where `DESIGN.md` says 400; the lock icon is 12 px inside a 10 px mark; `protocolOf` could be `Tab.protocol`.
- Ctrl+Shift+W with the vault view open closes an invisible tab.
- Prompts: a keyboard-interactive round with zero prompts has no focus target; the needs-vault busy flag resets before the resume (double click); `PasswordField` `shown` is not reset after a wrong password; the `FOCUSABLE` selector omits `textarea` and `select`.

blocks.title: Source: RDP TLS: own verifier, distinct errors, cause logging
blocks.text: From the review of the TLS handshake fix (PR #25, after v0.2.0): the fix keeps the handshake signature check (verified in the ironrdp-tls 0.3.0 and rustls 0.23.46 sources) but goes through the strict webpki verifier, so (1) a host whose certificate webpki cannot use now fails with `tls_failed` where it used to connect: RSA keys under 2048 or over 8192 bits, SHA-1 signatures, an unknown critical extension, a non-v3 certificate (old Windows, xrdp, embedded RDP servers); (2) an empty platform root store (a minimal Linux install without ca-certificates) makes every connect fail with `tls_failed` although roots play no part in the pin design; (3) `connect.rs` drops the cause of a TLS error, which makes (1) and (2) hard to tell apart (the new test asserts only `tls_failed`). Candidates: an own `ServerCertVerifier` that accepts the chain and checks signatures through the crypto provider, a distinct error code for the missing root store, debug logging of the cause without secrets. Check first with a real Windows 11 host (owner check, `cargo test -p fernjo-rdp --test connect` with `FERNJO_TEST_RDP_ADDR`) and, if available, an older or xrdp host.

blocks.title: Source: RDP: cap static channel reassembly
blocks.text: From the v0.2.0 release security review (Medium): ironrdp-svc reassembles static virtual channel data (clipboard, drdynvc) against a declared length that is never capped, so a hostile RDP server can make fernjo buffer gigabytes before the 1 MiB clipboard cap applies, and the app is killed for lack of memory. Needs a cap upstream or a limit on the bytes read per PDU in the transport. Mitigation today: switch the connection's clipboard off for hosts you do not trust. Also: a server that stops reading can keep a closing session alive (`writer.write_all` outside the `select!` in `crates/fernjo-rdp/src/session.rs`, no write timeout, unbounded `ops` channel in `src-tauri/src/sessions/rdp.rs`).

blocks.title: Source: RDP clipboard default and indicator
blocks.text: From the v0.2.0 release security review (Medium, design): the RDP clipboard is on by default and syncs the local clipboard to the remote host when the desktop gets focus, without a paste; the remote side can overwrite the local clipboard. Decide whether the default should be off or sync only on a paste, and whether a visible indicator is needed.

blocks.title: Source: RDP review Low items
blocks.text: From the v0.2.0 release security review: `build_config` puts the password into IronRDP's plain-`String` config without zeroize (API limit); `desktop_size` clamps each side to 8192 but not the area, so a very large tab makes `Framebuffer::new` fail with `desktop_too_large` instead of scaling down; the no-secret guard has no sentinel for an RDP user name or domain and its `rdp_input` and `rdp_clipboard` entries only reach the `session_not_connected` path; `app_menu.rs` uses a predictable temp name `<file>.<pid>.tmp` (`create_new`, so a planted file only causes an error) and does not require `APPIMAGE` to be absolute; `cert_store.rs` copies the `.bak` with `fs::copy` to a fixed name, as the `known_hosts` writer does.

blocks.title: Source: Clean the username of JSON and backup imports
blocks.text: From the v0.1.1 release security review (Low): `fernjo_import::limits::sanitize_nodes` cleans name, description and host of JSON and backup imports but not `settings.username`, which comes straight from the file (mRemoteNG usernames are cut to 256 characters at read time). A hostile file could put control characters or a very long string there; it renders as plain text and ends up as the SSH user name, with no code execution or secret exposure. Apply the same cap and cleaning as for the other fields.

blocks.title: Source: Atomic writers: `.bak` symlink and `connections.json` temp name
blocks.text: The M7 hardening gave `vault.fernjo` and `known_hosts` a random temp file name created with `create_new`, but the `.bak` step of all three atomic writers (`write_atomic` in `crates/fernjo-vault/src/vault.rs`, `crates/fernjo-ssh/src/known_hosts.rs` and `crates/fernjo-core/src/persist.rs`) still runs `fs::copy(path, &bak)` and `owner_only(&bak)`, which follow a symlink planted at the `.bak` name; `persist::write_atomic` (`connections.json`, `settings.json`) also still writes through the fixed `<file>.tmp` name, opened with create and truncate. Exploiting either needs write access to the data folder (a peer or a sync tool that syncs symlinks), so it is not a regression, but "followed through symlinks" is only fixed for the temp file. Fix options: remove an existing `.bak` symlink before copying, or write the `.bak` through the `create_new` plus rename helper; use a random temp name with `create_new` for `connections.json`. See `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, "M7: vault Low findings triage" (Limits).

blocks.title: Source: `clear_pending` residue after an overlapping failed apply
blocks.text: `AppState::clear_pending` uses `try_lock` and skips while an `import_apply` holds the lock; if that apply then fails, its pending value survives the page load that happened meanwhile. The next `import_begin` replaces it and the UI cannot apply it without one, so the effect is small. An optional fix is an `AtomicBool` set by the page-load hook that `import_apply` checks when it fails.

blocks.title: Source: `check-no-build-paths.sh` false-clean on grep error
blocks.text: `tools/check-no-build-paths.sh` runs without `-e` and counts matches with `n="$(grep -a -c -F -e "$pattern" "$bin")"` followed by `${n:-0}`, so a grep that fails with exit status 2 (unreadable file, I/O error) yields an empty count that reads as zero and the check passes. Capture grep's exit status and fail on anything above 1; add a test in `tools/test-release-scripts.sh`.

milestones.title: Automatic updates
milestones.goal: The app notices that a new version is available, shows it in the UI, and one click downloads, verifies and installs it in an app-themed update window and starts the new version.

tasks.text: Create spec `Docs/superpowers/specs/<date>-m13-auto-update-design.md` through brainstorming: update source and endpoint, check timing, privacy of the request, how each platform hands over to the installer (Windows NSIS exits the app, macOS replaces the `.app`, Linux updates the AppImage in place), what happens for a `.deb` or a read-only install location, handling and loss of the update signing key, and what the themed window can show while the installer runs

Update signing key pair (`tauri signer generate`, minisign): the public key goes into `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, the private key and its password exist as GitHub Actions secrets and in the owner's own copy, and are never in the repository, a log or an artifact; record how a lost or leaked key is handled (installs cannot update across a key change, so it needs a manual reinstall) in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`

Release workflow: the platform build jobs also produce and sign the update artifacts (NSIS installer, macOS `.app.tar.gz`, AppImage), a script in `tools/` writes `latest.json` (version, release notes, per platform URL and signature) and `tools/verify-installers.sh` checks it; both are attached to the draft release; the signing secret is available only to the step that signs, the pull request dry run (and every fork) builds without the key and skips signing; `tools/check-workflows.sh` stays green and `tools/test-release-scripts.sh` covers the new scripts

Rust side in `src-tauri/src/updater.rs` (no logic in TypeScript): update plugin with the endpoint and public key pinned to this repository’s release feed (HTTPS only), check at start after a short delay and every 24 hours, a manual check, only a strictly newer stable version (no downgrade, no pre-release), download with progress events, signature verified before anything is installed, install and restart through the same close confirmation as the other restarts ("Install update?" when sessions are connected; never `AppHandle::restart` directly); commands `update_check`, `update_install`, `update_skip`, status event `update-status`; they count in the three-places rule and have `table()` entries

Setting `checkForUpdates` in `settings.json` (default on) with a "Check now" button and the installed version in Settings; a scratch run with `FERNJO_DATA_DIR` never checks automatically (a manual run must not talk to the real feed); an unreadable `settings.json` keeps the check off with the specific note, not the generic one

UI (presentation only, follows `DESIGN.md` and the tokens): an "Update available" marker in the sidebar footer, an update window (`UpdateDialog.svelte`) with the new version, the release notes as plain text (never HTML), "Update and restart", "Later" and "Skip this version", a progress bar with the stage (downloading, verifying, installing, restarting), an error state with Retry and a link to the release page; no update path for a `.deb` or an install location that cannot be written: the window offers the release page instead

Narrow the webview capability (moved from the backlog; the update commands touch the same file): `src-tauri/capabilities` replaces `core:default` with `core:event:allow-listen` and `core:event:allow-unlisten` and the permissions the app really needs, checked in a real release build (not a debug harness), pinned in `src-tauri/tests/tauri_conf.rs`; the test that forbids an updater in the bundle config becomes a test that pins exactly this updater configuration (public key, endpoint, no other endpoint)

Privacy and docs: `README.md` and `SECURITY.md` state the update check (one HTTPS request to the release feed, no account, no identifiers beyond what the request itself carries, off with one setting), `Docs/release-checklist.md` drops the statement "No update check", `Docs/DECISIONS.md` records the choices, `CLAUDE.md` the lasting facts, `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` gets a short user-readable entry

Writer in `crates/fernjo-import` (`mremoteng/write.rs`, no Tauri, no I/O on app data), mirroring the reader: folders become containers, SSH becomes SSH2, RDP stays RDP, name, host, port, user, domain, description, RDP resolution, colour depth and clipboard map to their attributes, and every fernjo inheritance (node, folders upward, default) is written so each connection resolves to the same values in mRemoteNG as in fernjo (faithful per-setting mapping, like the import); the XML is escaped by the writer, never assembled from raw strings

blocks.title: Open manual checks (owner): M9
blocks.text:
**Run on 2026-11-23 by the owner on a Windows 11 PC and a macOS laptop; M9 was closed on that run.** The owner reported that every check below passed, with these exceptions and limits: check e found a wrong notice wording (fixed in pull request #44); the owner gave no per-step detail; **not run: the Linux Secret Service keychain item and any Linux device (the CachyOS laptop), a real-app look at the Sync UI on Linux, and the Podman `systemctl --user stop` timing, which the owner did not report.** The Quadlet unit did not start at first because `Init=true` is not a Quadlet key (`RunInit=true` is; fixed in pull request #43), and the hub needed `PublishPort=<hub VM LAN address>:8787:8787` instead of `127.0.0.1` because Caddy runs on another VM (Caddy answered 502, `connection refused`, before). Still worth doing on Linux before the release: the keychain item (set up, restart, leave sync, item gone) and one sync run from the CachyOS laptop.

**Two-device run (the manual criteria of M9).** On two of {gaming PC, CachyOS laptop, macOS 15 laptop}, against the hub VM (rootless Podman, Caddy `tls internal`, `benjo.loc`; setup in `Docs/hub.md`). Run on the Windows 11 PC and the macOS laptop; evidence on the two criteria of M9.

- a: set up device 1 (Settings, Sync), join device 2 with the pairing code.
- b: create and edit a connection on one device and see it on the other.
- c: add a vault entry on one and use it on the other (connect with it).
- d: take one device off the network, edit the same connection field on both and a different one on each, reconnect: one conflict copy and no loss.
- e: delete a connection on one while editing it on the other: it stays.
- f: restart the hub container and Caddy: nothing lost.
- g: restore the hub from an older VM snapshot: the devices refuse with the rolled-back notice and Re-seed rebuilds it.
- h: `fernjo-hub rotate-secret`: the old devices report `hub_unauthorized` until the secret is edited.

**Other owner checks:**

- Podman and Quadlet: `podman build -f crates/fernjo-hub/Containerfile -t fernjo-hub .`, then run it per `Docs/hub.md` and the Quadlet unit (`RunInit=true`, `UserNS=keep-id:uid=10001,gid=10001`, volume with `:Z`), `systemctl --user stop` ends it within a second. The fixer built and ran the image with Docker (`init`, a `docker stop` test, a writable fresh volume as user 10001); that is not a Podman or Quadlet check.
- Real keychains: `OsSyncSecrets` (the hub secret and the sync key under `sync-<group id>`, service `fernjo`) on Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain and the Linux Secret Service: set up, restart, sync still works, then leave sync and check that the item is gone. Run by the owner on Windows 11 and macOS on 2026-11-23, reported as passed; Linux not run.
- Caddy `tls internal` with the pinned CA PEM against the real hub: join with the CA PEM in the pairing code. The pinned-CA path is tested against a throwaway CA in `crates/fernjo-sync/tests/client_tls.rs` only.
- The close push (up to 3 s) and the window-focus trigger in the real app: edit a connection and close the window at once, then check the other device; focus the window after an edit on the other device.
- The UI in the real app (no WebView2 runtime on the development machine, so only a Chromium harness with a mocked API was used): the Sync section in Settings, the footer line, the join confirmation and the notices at 1280x800 in both themes.
- Code that only CI compiles: the Unix-only tests (hub signal handling `sigterm_and_sigint_end_the_wait`, symlink and fsync tests) and the Linux and macOS code paths; they run in the GitHub Actions jobs on the pull request, `gh pr checks`.

backlog.title: M11 review leftovers
backlog.text: Minor findings of the M11 task and wave reviews that were not fixed (the others went into wave K). `fernjo-fs` and the readers: the exhausted eight-attempt path of `create_temp_file` has no test; an oversize `Unreadable` reason says "the file is too large" instead of naming the cap, and the vault maps any `InvalidData` from `read_capped` to "larger than N MiB" (name the cap in `fernjo-fs`); `persist::write_atomic` copies the contents to append a newline (twice the memory near the cap); the backup-step temp file can stay next to `known_hosts` or `rdp_certs.confirmed` after a crash; no test pins the sync oversize text remap. RDP: `ChannelIds.statics` does not exclude the io and message channel ids (only a false-positive close reason); a cached pointer index of 32 or more is refused although harmless; no fake-server test for a TLS 1.2-only server, the provider assertion in the `tls.rs` tests cannot fail and they use `rustls::internal`; the comment above `install_ops` in `sessions/rdp.rs` is stale and the writer step is not unit-tested; `a_cancelled_handshake_leaves_no_session_task` uses a fixed 300 ms sleep; held remote clipboard text is written on focus after a disconnect; the clipboard marker also shows on restored or dropped RDP tabs (gate it on connected or word it "Clipboard on for"), treats `state_unusable` as on and misses an empty host. Import: a skipped reload during inspect or pick is not consumed; no test for the `import_begin` reset or the damaged-backup reset; the report text "name, description or host" omits user names and a cleaned mRemoteNG host or name is not reported; other format characters (U+200B, U+2060, U+FEFF) pass `clean`. App: `vault_lock` duplicates the `no_vault` and `vault_unusable` mapping of `with_vault`; the idle test swaps the global panic hook; a failed keychain `get` is not cached (a locked Secret Service is asked again); the `note_activity` command can block the main thread while an overdue lock waits on `pending`. Sync: `seq_exhausted` has no wording in `sync-errors.ts`; `Vault::file_bytes` checks the header only, so a damaged body under the right header is still pushed (a denial of service until the next good push, noted in DECISIONS); the 20 s wall-clock bound of the linear-time merge test can flake on a slow runner. UI: show the OSC 8 link target on hover (it is no longer shown anywhere). Tooling: the host key prompt test `time_spent_on_the_host_key_prompt...` (500 ms budget) flakes under parallel load; unanchored `.gitignore` names could hide a future fixture; a redundant `settings.json.bak`.

backlog.title: macOS: Cmd+Q likely skips the close confirmation
backlog.text: Read in the dependency sources on 2026-11-27, not run on a Mac: the default macOS menu's Quit sends `terminate:`, which raises no `RunEvent::ExitRequested`, so connected sessions would end without the "Close fernjo?" dialog (M10) and an update install would not hold the quit (M13). Check on the Mac first (Cmd+Q with a connected session); a fix is an own Quit menu item or an `applicationShouldTerminate:` hook. Details: `Docs/DECISIONS.md` "M10 quit confirmation on ExitRequested". For the M14 gate to triage.
